text.text: Run the studio from one page: clients, the packages you sell, every shoot from inquiry to delivered gallery, and the checklist that gets each one finished on time. Open the Dashboard each morning, then work Mine and the late galleries view. Chase every unpaid deposit before the shoot date.

The packages the studio sells, with what each one includes.
Each booked session from inquiry to gallery delivery.
Prep, shooting and editing steps for each shoot.

This workspace runs a photography studio's business side: every inquiry and client, the packages you sell, each shoot with its contract, deposit and balance, the to-do list from questionnaire to gallery, and delivery dates you promised. Your editing software and gallery host stay where they are; this is where bookings and promises are kept.

text.text: The Ashgrove family session is in two days. The questionnaire is back, so the photographer checks the sunset time, confirms the park, and sends a short note on what to wear.
Even a solo studio has two jobs: the photographer and the office. Block office time each week for replies, contracts and invoices, so editing days stay free.

text.text: Most inquiries are lost to slow replies, not to price. Answer fast, make the next step easy, and hold no date without a contract and deposit.
The first reply (within a few hours)
and the date of the first inquiry.
Thank them by name and mention one detail from their message.
Share the package that fits, with its starting price, and offer a short call.
Add a shoot row with status
and the date they asked about.
What the day or session is for, and what they want to remember
Location, timing and how many people
Their budget, asked plainly and kindly
For brands: where the images will be used, so the right image use is quoted
The package, what it includes, the delivery time and the image use.
The deposit to book and when the balance is due.
A reply-by date. Dates are first come, first served.
Follow up once after three days and once after a week. Then mark the inquiry closed with a note. Never chase more than twice.
If the price is the obstacle, offer a smaller package or a shorter session, not a discount on the same work. Discounts teach clients that your prices are negotiable.
The Brennans asked about an engagement session three days ago. The studio sends two package options with a reply-by date and offers a 15-minute call this week.
Use the same contract for every booking of a kind, with the package, date, deposit, balance due, delivery time, image use and cancellation terms filled in.
each quarter. If venue partners send most of the booked weddings, spend more time with venues and less on posting.
A calm shoot comes from preparation done days before. Clients notice when you know the timeline, the light and their names.
Timeline agreed for weddings and events, minute by minute
Must-have shot list confirmed, including family groupings
Location scouted at the same time of day, or checked with the venue
Second shooter confirmed if the package includes one
Balance invoice sent if the contract says it is due before the day
Check the weather and agree a backup plan for rain.
Send the client a short note: arrival time, where to meet, what to bring.
Confirm parking and any venue rules about flash or where you may stand.

Arrive early; walk the location and test the light.
For groups, have someone from the family call names so you can focus on the photos.
At the end, thank the client and tell them when to expect a sneak peek.
Back up every card twice before you go to bed; mark the backup task done.
Send a few preview images within 48 hours. It is the moment clients share you with friends.
The Whitfield wedding needs a second shooter and the questionnaire is not back yet. The studio sends a friendly reminder and books the ceremony lighting scout for the week before the day.
Bring water and a small kit for clients: hair ties, safety pins, tissues and a lint roller. For newborn sessions, warm the room and never pose a baby in a way that is not safe.
Ask for one contact on the day who is not the couple: a friend or the planner. They solve the small problems so the couple can enjoy the day.
The gallery is what clients keep and share. Deliver it on time, in a consistent style, with a short guide to what they can do with it.

Keep two copies of every delivered gallery for at least a year, one away from the studio. Clients lose files; a quick resend makes a loyal client.

The Whitfield engagement gallery was due a day ago and retouching is still in progress. The photographer emails the couple with a new date, sends three finished favorites as a thank-you, and delivers the full set within two days.
Tell the client before the date passes, with a new date you will keep. Clients forgive a short delay; they do not forgive silence.
Clear packages make booking easy, and deposits protect your calendar. Price for your time, not just the hours behind the camera.

text.text: A one-hour session takes far more than one hour: the inquiry and call, travel, shooting, culling, editing, delivery and admin. Count all of it. A family session often takes six to eight hours in total.
Taken when the contract is signed; nothing is held without it.
Usually not refundable, because you turned other work away for that date. Say so in the contract.

On the day or before delivery

text.text: when it arrives. No gallery goes out with a balance owing, unless the agreement says otherwise.

Price the image use separately. A business using images in advertising gets far more value than a family hanging a print, and the price should reflect that. Write the use on the package and in the delivery email.
Put your rescheduling rule in the contract: one free move with enough notice, after that a fee or a new deposit. Apply it the same way to everyone.
Review prices each year. When you are booked solid months ahead, it is time to raise them for new bookings.

The brand story day asks for half the fee to book, because it holds a full weekday and includes full commercial use. The Kestrel spring menu stills are booked on the same package, with the balance due on delivery.
